text: Bankr agents earn fees when their token trades. They still run out of compute. A hundred and five agents on Base have earned five hundred and ninety-three WETH, and burned nineteen billion LLM tokens in thirty days. Nothing lets them borrow against fees they already made.

Gadai is Indonesian for pledge. Every trade of a Bankr token pays creator fees to a beneficiary, and Doppler ships the call that moves them: updateBeneficiary. Gadai points that share at a per-loan vault. That is the lien. The vault sells FeeNotes for USDC, and only release gives the fee rights back.

The same engine prices every Bankr agent on Base, live. Over eight hundred and fifty dollars of credit across fourteen agents: fee history from Bankr's API, compute burn from its LLM Gateway. Each row shows the line, whether fees cover compute, and if not, why.

Some Bankr agents launched on Robinhood Chain, and three are paid creator fees in tokenized stocks: SPY, TSLA, MSTR. Gadai prices that stream in shares, quoted through Uniswap on chain forty-six sixty-three. Those lines are indicative, so we proved the leg for real: bridged with Relay, and bought a fraction of a Tesla share.

Underwriting is deterministic first. The engine takes the lowest of the seven-day, thirty-day and lifetime fee rates, haircut for lumpiness. That is the cap. Three persona agents then write memos on Bankr's LLM Gateway; the lead is binding and can only lower it. The skeptic cuts this one to seventy-nine dollars. And before approving, the desk pays five cents over x402 for a honeypot verdict. Honeypot declines the loan. Suspicious halves it.

Here is a real one. Two hundred and thirty-seven dollars against GITLAWB's fees. The borrower brought its own ERC-8004 identity, then called updateBeneficiary: fifty-seven percent of the token's fee share moved into the loan's vault. That is the lien.

The debt itself becomes an asset. Each loan mints a FeeNote that redeems one-for-one in USDC as fees arrive, and lenders buy it in a Uniswap Continuous Clearing Auction. It raises the whole principal, or it does not fund. The desk's Dynamic wallet places the anchor bid.

Then it runs itself. The Dynamic wallet disburses. The keeper collects the fees the pool accrued, swaps WETH to USDC through the Uniswap Trading API, and repays the noteholders. Debt hits zero, release returns the fee rights, and the desk writes repayment reputation to the borrower's ERC-8004 identity. Every desk transaction carries a Base builder code.

Gadai's customers are other agents. It sells the same credit report on Bankr's x402 Cloud for two cents a call; unpaid requests get a 402. It buys its risk data the same way, and it installs as a skill: the Bankr Skill borrows by chat, two Grok Bot skills watch the board and a live loan.

Every credit decision is a public, scored signal, with a share card for X and a live Flash quote for the order a follower would place. Auto-mirroring uses Dynamic delegated access, configured and waiting on one user approval. A mirror is a market buy with a take-profit bracket, or a DCA from a Flash TWAP; ten basis points goes to Gadai. And it follows itself: a real Flash TWAP on Base mainnet, first slice filled.

A loan is money an agent can spend: every loan carries a dining budget. The concierge ranks against it on Blackbird's live production data, what the network checked into this week, and all sixteen hundred and seventy-five venues. Paying in FLY is pending Blackbird's review, so Gadai moves no money. A member logs in for their passport; the plan returns tonight's hours, a cost estimate, and how busy each place is.

None of this is a mock. On Base mainnet FeeDesk is deployed, the desk is ERC-8004 agent ninety-four six ninety-nine, the x402 payment and the Flash order are on-chain. Every page says what ran where, and the desk's Dynamic MPC wallet signed all of it.

Honestly: Bankr's data, the mainnet contracts, the x402 payments and the Flash order are live. The lifecycle runs on an Anvil fork of Base against a real Bankr pool, because a pledge moves real fee rights. Every page says which is which. Gadai: credit for agents, secured by fees they already earn.
